title: The --unbound pre-check binds the emitter's fallback names (Header as Hdr), which disagree with a Go-derived codec model's (R_Header), so bindable laws are recorded UNKNOWN without being decided
reproduction: I121's attempt 3 (the PAR job under --unbound unknown, Q105) recorded 89 of its 97 laws UNKNOWN as unbindable, 87 of them decided in the committed M3 records. holon/codecrun.py binds records.ir_roots_text(law) before deciding; its types01 maps a Header binder, and every field term, to Hdr; gen/M3/model/header_length.bend defines R_Header and has no Hdr. Attempt 2, without the flag, decided the same statements, and the post-decision check binds res['statement_text']. Confirmed by reading the code on the lead (538a9312); not re-run. The same pre-check runs in every composed corpus run since I115 (the base protocol's run_unbound "unknown"): in I122's counted run 234 of the 268 derived laws are recorded UNKNOWN by the binding check (c04 134, c09 32, c06 28, c14 28, c19 9, c03 1, c08 1, c18 1; the corpus.json run stage's binding_unknown), an upper bound on this defect's effect, since a genuinely unbindable law counts there too.
suggested_fix: In the pre-check, bind the statement text the emitter produces without deciding, falling back to ir_roots_text only where the emitter refuses; planted fixtures for a model that defines R_<Type> and for F-M6-05's unbindable shape.

round: the lead, at I124's landing (HUMAN_ANSWERS Q115 (5)); found by I121's refacts dry run on attempt 4's assembled tree
title: A trace's directory listings record whether bytecode caches exist: SKIP filters __pycache__ paths, not the __pycache__ entry inside a recorded listing, so trace.check depends on the tree's bytecode state
reproduction: Python's import system lists each package directory it imports from (an os.listdir audit event), and holon.trace records that listing as the sha256 of its sorted names, __pycache__ included; SKIP is applied only to the listed directory's own path. Writing bytecode adds __pycache__ to the directory, so the same listing hashes differently before and after: the lead reproduced it on a scratch package (2 listdir events during two imports; the listing hash moved from aa2bd39df497fec5 to 0b522936260c7900), and I121 on holon/bundle2 with an audit hook. trace.check (holon land's dirty detection, holon/land.py:551, and trace.reusable, holon/__main__.py:257) then reports 'listing of <dir> changed' whenever the bytecode state differs between the recording tree and the checking tree; CI sets no PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE. I121's refacts dry run on its assembled sandbox tree refused 106 of its 107 facts-form lines on assembly artifacts of that tree (__pycache__ entries in recorded listings, and #212's fix overlaid on its code). Fail-closed: it only adds refusals and dirty laws, never a verdict.
suggested_fix: Filter SKIP-matching names out of a recorded listing and out of the check's, with planted fixtures (the same tree with and without __pycache__ checks equal; a real added or removed entry still fails). holon/trace.py is in every trace's code map, so its PR states the re-make scope before any code and never silently re-means an existing record.
fix_iteration: a fix PR of its own (I121's proposal, HUMAN_ANSWERS Q115 (5)), before the PR that lands I121's withheld re-decision
